user.title: Xolta battery (local Modbus)
user.description: Enter the IP address of the Xolta site controller. Give it a fixed IP address (DHCP reservation) in your router first.

data.allow_write: Allow Home Assistant to control the battery

data_description.host: The fixed IP address of the site controller, e.g. 192.168.1.50.
data_description.allow_write: Off = read only (safe). On = adds an override (Auto / Stop / Self-consumption) that writes to the battery. You can change this later under Configure.

modbus_closed.title: Modbus is not open yet
modbus_closed.description:
The battery controller answers at **{host}**, but Modbus is not open. Only Ebbefos/Xolta support can open it. Send this e-mail to **support@ebbefosenergy.dk**:

> **Subject:** Enable Modbus TCP
>
> Hello Ebbefos Energy,
>
> I have a Xolta battery (account: *your e-mail in the Ebbefos app*, site controller: *SCR-number from your router*, IP address: {host}).
>
> Could you enable the Modbus TCP server on the site controller (port 502)? I want to read the battery locally in Home Assistant. The IP address is reserved in my router.

You can save now: Home Assistant keeps checking and starts by itself once Modbus is open, and a repair notice is shown until then.

menu_options.wait: Save and wait (Home Assistant keeps checking)

data_description.host: The new fixed IP address of the site controller.

error.cannot_connect: Nothing answers at this address. Check the IP address, that the battery is on, and that Home Assistant can reach that network.
error.modbus_closed: The controller answers, but Modbus is not open. Ask Ebbefos/Xolta support to open it (see the README).
error.not_xolta: Something answered, but it does not look like a Xolta site controller.

abort.already_configured: This controller is already set up.
abort.reconfigure_successful: The IP address has been updated.

data.allow_write: Allow Home Assistant to control the battery
data.repeat_interval: Repeat interval while an override is active

data_description.allow_write: Turning this off removes the override entities and stops any active override. Nothing is written; the cloud takes control back by itself.
data_description.scan_interval: How often the battery is read. Default 10 s.
data_description.repeat_interval: The cloud resets the mode after about 90 s, so the override is written again at this interval. Default 20 s.

modbus_closed.title: Xolta battery: Modbus is not open
modbus_closed.description:
The battery controller answers at {host}, but Modbus does not. Either Modbus has not been opened yet, or it was closed (for example by a Xolta software update).

Ask Ebbefos/Xolta support (support@ebbefosenergy.dk) to enable the Modbus TCP server on port 502. The README has an e-mail you can copy.

Home Assistant keeps checking, and this notice disappears by itself once Modbus answers again.

controller_unreachable.title: Xolta battery: no answer from {host}
controller_unreachable.description:
Nothing answers at {host}. Check that the battery is on, that the controller still has this IP address (use a DHCP reservation), and that Home Assistant can reach that network. If the IP address changed, use Reconfigure on the integration.

This notice disappears by itself once the controller answers again.

set_override.name: Set override
set_override.description: Start or end a battery override. Auto writes nothing; the cloud takes control back within a few minutes.

duration.name: Duration
duration.description: Hours before Auto is restored. Default: the Override duration entity.

write_failed.message: Could not write to the battery: {error}
